one_liner: GitHub offers a broad REST API (plus GraphQL) with OAuth apps, GitHub Apps and PATs, and an official GitHub MCP server. Building on it needs no partnership.
auth_notes: The fetched REST docs navigation lists OAuth authorizations, fine-grained personal access tokens, and GitHub App installation and user tokens. GitHub App auth involves a JWT you mint yourself. The pages do not describe the flows in detail, so these details come from the section headings plus background knowledge.
access_notes: The fetched pages do not state pricing for API access. The Developer Program page says membership is open to individual developers, and the partner programs are optional and only for selling to enterprises. No fetched page makes the API conditional on a paid plan or partnership. Free self-serve access rests mainly on background knowledge.
blocker_notes: No blocker is evident in the fetched pages. The partner programs are optional, aimed at selling to enterprises, and not required to use the API. Some endpoints may depend on the plan of the underlying feature, which the pages do not settle.
